description: Registry wiring + list_available_models() (P2.10). Register all built-in ProviderFactories (OpenAI, LmStudio, GenericOpenAI, Azure, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock) at startup, and implement list_available_models() returning provider, model, capabilities, and price so the Phase 5 model selector has data. Add price sourcing (per Section 6.2: user-entered per-provider token rates in the versioned app config, seeded with optional bundled defaults per ProviderKind; local providers default to zero cost). Wire a list_available_models tauri command + register it, and mirror the new AvailableModel/Capabilities/ModelInfo shapes into frontend TS types. Do NOT build the model-selector UI (Phase 5). Depends on FEAT-001/002/003. providers crate compile/test/clippy DEFERRED TO CI; tauri-app also verified in CI.
steps: In crates/providers (registry.rs or a new builtins.rs): add a function that constructs a ProviderRegistry with all seven built-in factories registered (OpenAI, LmStudio, GenericOpenAI, Azure, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock), one per ProviderKind. Add a helper to build instances from a slice of persisted ProviderConfig rows.

Define an AvailableModel type (provider_id, model, capabilities: Capabilities, price: optional token pricing) in the providers crate (contract.rs or registry.rs), matching the Section 6.1 `AvailableModel` intent (provider/model + capabilities + price) so Phase 4 routing and Phase 5 UI can consume it. Implement `list_available_models()` on the registry (or a free fn taking the registry + configs + pricing table) that, for each configured provider instance, lists its models and attaches capabilities and price. Because list_models may hit the network, design it to accept injected/mocked model lists in tests. Local providers (LmStudio) default to zero price.

Add pricing config: extend persistence AppConfig (crates/persistence/src/config.rs) with an additive, optional per-provider/per-model token-rate table (e.g. a serde-default map keyed by provider kind or provider id, with input/output token rates and a last-edited marker) seeded with optional bundled defaults per ProviderKind, local=zero. Keep it forward-compatible (additive; existing AppConfig tests must still pass). This is the single source the cost signal and list_available_models both read (Section 6.2). If wiring the full config table proves large, at minimum define the price type in providers and thread an optional pricing map into list_available_models; document any deferral in findings.

In crates/tauri-app: add a `list_available_models` #[tauri::command] in commands.rs that assembles the registry from persisted ProviderConfig rows + pricing from AppConfig and returns Vec<AvailableModel> (display-safe: provider/model/capabilities/price only, NEVER secrets). Add a structured error path via the existing CommandError. Register the command in lib.rs `generate_handler!`. AppState may need an accessor to the providers repo/pricing; add minimally. Follow the existing command validation/error conventions. Do NOT expose any secret material or SecretStore::resolve.

Mirror the new shapes into hybrid-orchestrator/frontend/src/types/index.ts BY HAND (camelCase to match serde): add Capabilities (streaming, tools, vision, jsonMode, maxContext: number | null), ModelInfo, a ModelPrice/token-rate type, and AvailableModel (providerId, model, capabilities, price | null). Follow the existing file's conventions and comments; keep unions single-line if they fit in 100 cols. Update AppConfig's TS mirror if you extended it. Verify formatting with `NODE_OPTIONS= prettier --check .` from the frontend dir before finishing (global prettier; .prettierrc.json is doubleQuote/printWidth 100/trailingComma all/endOfLine lf).

Add tests: a providers-crate test proving the built-in registry registers all seven kinds and that list_available_models returns provider/model/capabilities/price for configured providers using INJECTED/mocked model lists (no live network). A persistence test for the pricing config round-trip (additive; existing config tests still pass). If feasible, a tauri-app command-body unit test (driving an extracted inner fn like the set_provider_secret pattern) proving list_available_models returns display-safe rows with no secret material.

Run `cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/providers/Cargo.toml` and `cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/tauri-app/Cargo.toml`. Offline: run `cargo build/test/clippy --workspace` (offline members incl. persistence's config change is under an excluded crate so verify persistence via its --manifest-path fmt only offline; its compile/test is CI). Run `cargo test --manifest-path crates/persistence/Cargo.toml` is CI-only (crates.io). Confirm frontend `NODE_OPTIONS= prettier --check .` passes. Note in findings what compiled offline vs deferred to CI (providers, tauri-app, persistence config change all CI-verified).
acceptance_criteria: A built-in registry constructor registers all seven ProviderFactories (OpenAI, LmStudio, GenericOpenAI, Azure, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock).
list_available_models() returns provider_id, model, capabilities, and price for configured providers; local providers default to zero price; tests use injected/mocked model lists (no live network).
Pricing is sourced from the versioned AppConfig (additive, forward-compatible) seeded with optional per-kind defaults; existing AppConfig tests still pass.
A `list_available_models` #[tauri::command] exists, is registered in generate_handler!, returns only display-safe data (no secrets), and follows existing command/error conventions.
frontend/src/types/index.ts mirrors Capabilities/ModelInfo/ModelPrice/AvailableModel (and any AppConfig change) in camelCase; `NODE_OPTIONS= prettier --check .` passes.
No model-selector UI is built (Phase 5 scope respected).
Offline members build/test/clippy green; providers + tauri-app + persistence config change deferred to CI as documented.
verification: From hybrid-orchestrator/: `cargo build --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (offline members)

`cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/providers/Cargo.toml --check` and `cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/tauri-app/Cargo.toml --check` and `cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/persistence/Cargo.toml --check`
Review confirms list_available_models returns provider/model/capabilities/price, is registered, exposes no secrets, and TS mirror matches; providers/tauri-app/persistence compile+test deferred to CI.
findings:
IMPLEMENTED (P2.10):
- providers/src/builtins.rs (new): `builtin_registry()` registers all seven ProviderFactories (OpenAI, LmStudio, GenericOpenAI, Azure, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock), one per ProviderKind; `build_registry(configs, secrets)` layers on instances from persisted ProviderConfig rows. Added `TokenPrice{input_per_mtok,output_per_mtok}` (camelCase, f64/1M-tok, ZERO const + Default), `PricingTable` (per-kind BTreeMap + per-(kind,model) override map; `bundled_defaults()` seeds cloud kinds nonzero and local kinds/GenericOpenAI to zero; `price_for` falls back per-model->per-kind->ZERO), and `AvailableModel{provider_id,model,capabilities,price}` (camelCase, DISPLAY-SAFE). `list_available_models(&registry,&configs,&pricing)` is async, drives ChatProvider::list_models() per instance (matched to its config row for kind), attaches capabilities(model)+price; instances lacking a config row are skipped. Tests inject a FakeProvider with fixed model lists (no network).
- providers/src/registry.rs: added `insert_instance(Arc<dyn ChatProvider>)` so tests (and out-of-band builds) can register a prebuilt instance without a factory.
- providers/src/lib.rs: wired `pub mod builtins;` and re-exported build_registry/builtin_registry/list_available_models/AvailableModel/PricingTable/TokenPrice.
- domain/src/models.rs: ProviderKind now also derives Hash + PartialOrd + Ord (additive) so it can key the registry HashMap (pre-existing use) and the ordered BTreeMap pricing tables. NOTE: registry.rs already used HashMap<ProviderKind,_> so Hash was in fact required for the providers crate to compile in CI; this derive makes that correct.
- persistence/src/config.rs: extended AppConfig with additive `pricing: PricingConfig` (#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if=PricingConfig::is_empty)] so empty is omitted -> older configs and existing tests unaffected). Added `TokenRate` (mirrors providers::TokenPrice camelCase) and `PricingConfig{per_kind: BTreeMap<ProviderKind,TokenRate>, per_model: BTreeMap<ProviderKind,BTreeMap<String,TokenRate>>, last_edited: Option<DateTime<Utc>>}`. This is the single source both the cost signal and list_available_models read (Section 6.2). Updated the existing save_then_load test constructor for the new field; added `empty_pricing_is_omitted_from_serialized_config` and `pricing_config_round_trips_additively` tests. Existing tests (load_defaults_when_empty, unknown_newer_fields_are_preserved_on_load) unchanged and still valid (extra catch-all still flattens).
- tauri-app/src/commands.rs: added `list_available_models` #[tauri::command] + extracted `list_available_models_inner(&AppState)` (set_provider_secret_inner testability pattern). It loads ProviderConfig rows via ProviderRepo over session_manager.db(), loads AppConfig pricing, converts via `pricing_table_from_config`, builds the registry (resolving api_key_ref through secret_store at build time), and returns Vec<AvailableModel>. DISPLAY-SAFE: only provider/model/capabilities/price cross IPC; SecretStore::resolve is NEVER wired to the return path. Structured CommandError::internal error path. Registered in lib.rs generate_handler!. Tests: list_available_models_inner_empty_when_no_providers, pricing_table_from_config_threads_rates_and_zeros_unpriced, available_model_is_display_safe.
- orchestrator-core/src/lib.rs: the smoke test called the now-removed `providers::placeholder()` (FEAT-001 replaced the providers placeholder with real modules, leaving this reference stale and CI-breaking). Updated it to reference the real `providers::builtin_registry()` + assert a factory is registered.
- frontend/src/types/index.ts: hand-mirrored Capabilities (streaming/tools/vision/jsonMode/maxContext:number|null), ModelInfo (id/displayName/contextLength), TokenPrice (inputPerMtok/outputPerMtok), AvailableModel (providerId/model/capabilities/price), and PricingConfig (perKind/perModel Partial<Record<ProviderKind,...>>, lastEdited:string|null). AppConfig itself has no TS mirror in this file, so only the new IPC/config shapes were added.

VERIFIED OFFLINE:
- `cargo fmt --check` for providers, tauri-app, persistence, domain, orchestrator-core: PASS.
- `cargo build/test/clippy --workspace` (offline members mcp-client+routing only): PASS (clippy -D warnings clean; smoke test still references a real providers item and passes).
- frontend `NODE_OPTIONS= prettier --check .`: PASS.

DEFERRED TO CI (crates.io 403 offline; these crates are [workspace] exclude and cannot compile in the sandbox): compile/test/clippy for providers, persistence, tauri-app, domain, orchestrator-core via the existing per-manifest CI steps (ubuntu + windows). No new deps were added to any Cargo.toml (used existing chrono/serde/domain/providers/persistence path deps), so no version-literal sync was needed. No CI workflow edits required: build/clippy/test + fmt-check steps for all five touched crates already exist in .github/workflows/ci.yml. Model-selector UI intentionally NOT built (Phase 5).
